title: Harden worker Dockerfile Node tarball download with SHASUMS256 verification
description: The worker image (.devcontainer/Dockerfile, US-003/US-R3-002) downloads the Node.js tarball from nodejs.org over HTTPS with no checksum/signature verification. Reviewer SUGGESTION on PR #149 (CAM-201 round 4): add a curl of SHASUMS256.txt + sha256sum -c before extracting, to harden the supply chain and catch a corrupted/truncated download. Low-risk given HTTPS + pinned exact version; nice-to-have.

acceptanceCriteria: Before extracting, .devcontainer/Dockerfile verifies the Node tarball's sha256 against nodejs.org's published checksums: it fetches https://nodejs.org/dist/v${NODE_VERSION}/SHASUMS256.txt, selects the line for node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz, and runs sha256sum -c on it; the build fails-closed (non-zero, no extract) if the checksum does not match.

The checksum step keys off ${NODE_ARCH} (the same variable that builds the download URL, from dpkg --print-architecture at Dockerfile:37-42), never a hardcoded x64, so both amd64 (x64) and arm64 builds verify their own artifact.

The tarball is downloaded to its real filename node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz (not /tmp/node.tar.xz) so sha256sum -c matches the bare-filename entry in SHASUMS256.txt; the tar -xJf extract line (Dockerfile:45) is updated to the real path.

Both curls (the Node tarball and SHASUMS256.txt) use retry flags (--retry with a small count + --retry-connrefused/--retry-delay) and keep --fail, so a transient network flake retries instead of failing the build.

The ci-container job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:42-81), which fires because this change touches .devcontainer/**, builds the worker image successfully with the new verification step (container_changed=true path).
bun run typecheck, bun test, and bun run check:all pass green (the change is Dockerfile-only; the substantive verification is the ci-container image build).
spec.scope: Harden the worker image Node.js tarball download at .devcontainer/Dockerfile:43 with sha256sum -c against nodejs.org's SHASUMS256.txt plus curl --retry, to catch a corrupted/truncated/flaky download and fail closed. Strictly the Node tarball. NOT in scope: GPG signature verification (rejected on merit - would need importing/pinning/rotating the Node release keys, and is incoherent as a lone high-assurance step while the base image and npm install trust registry TLS; a coherent supply-chain hardening of the whole image would be a separate issue), base-image digest pinning (Dockerfile:16), the claude-code npm install hash (Dockerfile:58), and apt (Dockerfile:26-31) - those rely on their own signing and are noted only for awareness.
gotchas: SHASUMS256.txt lists BARE filenames, so download the tarball to its real filename (node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz) rather than /tmp/node.tar.xz, or sha256sum -c will mismatch on filename; update the subsequent tar -xJf path to match.
The checksum grep/filename MUST use ${NODE_ARCH} (already in scope in the same RUN block), not a hardcoded x64, or the arm64 build breaks.

The build is single-arch per invocation (buildDockerBuildArgv in src/supervisor/worker-container.ts:231-253 emits a plain docker build, no buildx / --platform / TARGETARCH); NODE_ARCH comes from dpkg --print-architecture at build time.

No test asserts Dockerfile text content; verification is the ci-container image build succeeding on the .devcontainer/** change (the macOS ci job has no Docker daemon - the CAM-178 trap). Since CI will not deliberately corrupt the tarball, the reviewer confirms fail-closed behaviour by inspection, not by an automated failing case.

There is no existing --retry / sha256sum -c convention in the repo; this introduces the first, consistent with the pinned-reproducible-toolchain intent already documented in the Dockerfile header (lines 1-13, 33-35).
